content.text: /ext:medcp What is the most frequent diagnosis among women in their 50s in our cohort?
I'll query the clinical records. First, let me see the available tables and their structure.

This is an OMOP CDM database. I'll find women (gender) currently in their 50s (age 50–59), then find their most frequent condition. Let me query, joining condition occurrences to concepts for readable names.

arguments.sql_query:
SELECT c.concept_name AS diagnosis, COUNT(*) AS occurrence_count, COUNT(DISTINCT p.person_id) AS distinct_patients
FROM omop.person p
JOIN omop.condition_occurrence co ON co.person_id = p.person_id
JOIN omop.concept c ON c.concept_id = co.condition_concept_id
WHERE p.gender_concept_id = 8532
  AND (EXTRACT(YEAR FROM co.condition_start_date) - p.year_of_birth) BETWEEN 50 AND 59
GROUP BY c.concept_name
ORDER BY occurrence_count DESC
LIMIT 20;

content.text: SQL Server backend. I'll use `YEAR()` and `DATEPART` instead of `EXTRACT`.

arguments.sql_query:
SELECT TOP 20 c.concept_name AS diagnosis, COUNT(*) AS occurrence_count, COUNT(DISTINCT p.person_id) AS distinct_patients
FROM omop.person p
JOIN omop.condition_occurrence co ON co.person_id = p.person_id
JOIN omop.concept c ON c.concept_id = co.condition_concept_id
WHERE p.gender_concept_id = 8532
  AND (YEAR(co.condition_start_date) - p.year_of_birth) BETWEEN 50 AND 59
GROUP BY c.concept_name
ORDER BY occurrence_count DESC;

The most frequent diagnosis among women in their 50s in the cohort is **Primary malignant neoplasm of breast**, with 344,661 condition occurrences (6,740 distinct patients).

A caveat on interpretation: ranking by raw occurrence count favors chronically-tracked conditions. If you care about *how many women* are affected rather than total records, the picture changes:

| Diagnosis | Occurrences | Distinct patients |
|---|---|---|
| Primary malignant neoplasm of breast | 344,661 | 6,740 |
| Essential hypertension | 305,629 | **39,203** |
| Hyperlipidemia | 189,627 | 28,317 |
| Type 2 diabetes mellitus | 163,508 | 11,226 |
| Chest pain | 134,152 | 24,339 |

By **distinct patients**, **essential hypertension** (39,203 women) is the most common diagnosis — breast cancer has more total records but far fewer individuals, reflecting a heavily oncology-weighted cohort with intensive repeat coding.
